questions.stem: The sound level is $L=10\log_{10}(I/I_0)$ decibels, where $I_0=10^{-12}$ W m$^{-2}$. Two incoherent machines produce levels of 72 dB and 68 dB at a fixed location. Their intensities, rather than their decibel levels, add.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the combined sound level when both machines operate.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The second machine is unchanged. Find the minimum percentage reduction in the first machine's intensity needed to make the combined level at most 70 dB.

steps.text: A 70 dB limit corresponds to total intensity $10^{-5}$ W m$^{-2}$.
$k=0.23285017$, so reduce the first intensity by at least $76.714983\%$.

questions.stem: The height of a small survey drone during a programmed flight is modelled by $h(t)=at^2+bt+c$, where $t$ is seconds after the flight starts and $h$ is metres above level ground. Measurements give $h(0)=2$, $h(2)=14$ and $h(5)=17$. The model is used only from the start until the first contact with ground level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $a,b,c$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the physical time domain of this model.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the maximum height predicted during this domain.

steps.text: Solve $-t^2+8t+2=0$ and retain the positive root.
The vertex is at $t=4$, giving maximum height $18$ m.

questions.stem:
Eighty delivery delays are grouped as shown. The histogram uses frequency density on the vertical axis.

| Delay $t$ / min | Frequency |
| --- | --- |
| $0\le t<5$ | 8 |
| $5\le t<15$ | 24 |
| $15\le t<30$ | 30 |
| $30\le t\le50$ | 18 |

For estimates inside a class, assume observations are uniformly distributed within that class.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the height of the bar for $30\le t\le50$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the median delay using linear interpolation.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Estimate the probability that a randomly selected delay exceeds 25 minutes.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: State the modal class indicated by the histogram.

steps.text: The density is $18/20=0.9$ observations per minute.
The median is the 40th cumulative observation, in the 15-to-30 class after 32 observations.
Use one third of the 30 observations in 15-to-30, plus all 18 in the last class.
The modal class is $5\le t<15$, which has the greatest frequency density.

questions.stem: A condition affects 8% of a population. Test 1 has sensitivity 0.90 and specificity 0.85; test 2 has sensitivity 0.95 and specificity 0.98. Sensitivity is the probability of a positive result given the condition; specificity is the probability of a negative result given no condition. For each person, the two test results are independent conditional on whether that person has the condition.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly selected person tests positive on both tests.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a person has the condition given two positive results.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine whether the two positive-test events are independent in the whole population. Support your answer numerically.

steps.text: Divide $0.08(0.90)(0.95)$ by the probability in part (a).
This differs from $P(+_1\cap+_2)=0.07116$, so the positive events are not unconditionally independent. Conditional independence does not imply unconditional independence.

questions.stem: Three existing monitoring stations are at $A(1,1)$, $B(9,1)$ and $C(5,7)$ km. A rectangular reserve has $0\le x\le10$ and $0\le y\le8$. A new station will be placed either at the Voronoi vertex $U$ equidistant from A,B,C, or at $V(5,8)$. The selected candidate should maximize its distance to the nearest existing station.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of $U$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the distance from each candidate to its nearest existing station.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Choose between the two candidates and state the relevant comparison.

steps.text: The perpendicular bisector of AB is $x=5$.
Equating distances to A and C gives $8x+12y=72$.
At U the nearest distance is $13/3$ km.
At V the nearest station is C, at distance $1$ km.
Choose U, since $13/3>1$. This compares only the two permitted candidates, not every point in the reserve.

questions.stem: A subscriber is either a regular user R or an occasional user O each month. The regular transition matrix, with columns denoting origin states, is $T=\begin{pmatrix}0.88&0.25\\0.12&0.75\end{pmatrix}$ in the order R,O. Initially $P(R)=0.15$. Let $p_n=P(R\text{ in month }n)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find a recurrence for $p_n$ and calculate $p_1$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the long-run regular-user probability.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the first month for which the regular-user probability is at least 0.65. Justify that it is the first.

steps.text: The first month is $7$; the sequence is increasing toward $p_*>0.65$.

questions.stem:
Eight independent sampled pairs $(x,y)$ are shown below. Assume they are a random sample from a bivariate normal population.

| $x$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | 10 | 13 | 12 | 18 | 17 | 20 | 21 | 24 |

Test for positive population correlation at the 1% significance level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State the hypotheses and find the one-tailed $p$-value.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State the statistical conclusion and explain why it is not a statement that $x$ causes $y$.

steps.text: Use all eight raw pairs in a Pearson calculation.
$p=4.2360842e-05<0.01$, so reject zero correlation in favour of positive correlation.
Even significant correlation does not identify a causal mechanism or remove possible common causes.

questions.stem:
A cumulative nutrient release $R$ (mg) is measured $t$ hours after treatment.

| $t$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R$ | 6.2 | 10.0 | 12.6 | 13.7 | 14.8 | 15.0 |

Two proposed models are $R_A=16(1-e^{-0.5t})$ and $R_B=-0.3t^2+3.5t+1$. Define each residual as observed minus predicted.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the residuals for model A and its sum of squared residuals.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the sum of squared residuals for model B. Select the model with the better fit by this criterion.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Compare the physical plausibility of the models for very large $t$, and give a reason for caution about using either model beyond the observed times.

steps.text: Evaluate model A at all six times and subtract from the observations.
Choose model A because its residual sum of squares is smaller.
A approaches 16 mg, whereas B eventually decreases and becomes negative, which is implausible for cumulative release.
The data only cover 1 to 6 hours; the long-term mechanism or environment may differ, so the better observed fit does not validate distant extrapolation.
